messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: compiling error: 'deep_copy' is not a member of 'stan::model'
parts:
Hi,

I have tested rstan for some simple spatial CAR models, and when I started to make the model more complicated, I came across this error, which gives me no clue where to debug...

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
WARNING: left-hand side variable (name=Sigma) occurs on right-hand side of assignment, causing inefficient deep copy to avoid aliasing.
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    u_1_2 ~ multi_normal(...)

Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) : 
  Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! file10ac208a5c06.cpp: In member function 'T__ model10ac2e11466f_two_var_namespace::model10ac2e11466f_two_var::log_prob(std::vector<T2>&, std::vector<int>&, std::ostream*) const':
file10ac208a5c06.cpp:665:29: error: 'deep_copy' is not a member of 'stan::model'
make: *** [file10ac208a5c06.o] Error 1
Warning message:
running command 'make -f "C:/R/R-32~1.2/etc/x64/Makeconf" -f "C:/R/R-32~1.2/share/make/winshlib.mk" -f "C:/Users/jdx66/Documents/.R/Makevars" SHLIB_LDFLAGS='$(SHLIB_CXXLDFLAGS)' SHLIB_LD='$(SHLIB_CXXLD)' SHLIB="file10ac208a5c06.dll" WIN=64 TCLBIN=64 OBJECTS="file10ac208a5c06.o"' had status 2 
In addition: Warning message:
running command 'C:/R/R-32~1.2/bin/x64/R CMD SHLIB file10ac208a5c06.cpp 2> file10ac208a5c06.cpp.err.txt' had status 1 

I think I can ignore the warnings:
the first one was happening because I was assigning one block of a matrix Sigma using the transpose of the other one. So the matrix Sigma is on both side of "<-".
the second warning is because I was stacking two vector u_1 and u_2 into u_1_2, so it's a nonlinear transformation, but that's what I want.

So how can I solve the compilation error? Is that related to the rep_row() operation I'm using? Or the elementwise .* operation? (since if I use a.*b, stan will say variable "a." not found, so I simply use "a .b" , just adding a space after "a".)

The code is attached for your information. Thanks.

Jiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] compiling error: 'deep_copy' is not a member of 'stan::model'
parts:
Thanks for pointing this out. It looks like there's
a case missing in the assignment operator. I'll try
to track down the cause when I have more time tomorrow and
file an issue and hopefully a quick fix.

To work around it, I'd suggest breaking things down into loops
and/or using the array/vector/matrix multi-indexing/slicing.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] compiling error: 'deep_copy' is not a member of 'stan::model'
parts:
I just found the thing causing the issue. 
Sigma[1:J1, (J1+1):(J1+J2)] <- gamma12 *(A_1_inv'*Psi_12*A_2_inv);
Sigma[(J1+1):(J1+J2), 1:J1] <- (Sigma[1:J1, (J1+1):(J1+J2)])';
This deep copy statement messed things up.
So I created a temporary variable to store the part and it can complied now.

Thank you Bob.

Jiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] compiling error: 'deep_copy' is not a member of 'stan::model'
parts:
Great --- glad you found a workaround.

I'll get in a fix for the copy. For those who care what's
going on under the hood, these copies are getting resolved
with recursive template functions in C++ that provide a kind
of built-in lazy copying. It looks like I missed and edge
case both in the code and the testing. The matrices in Eigen
are implemented separately from the vectors, so this should
be easy to fix.

Thanks again for reporting.

- Bob
